newsitem.title: USA: America Online sees unfair burden from FCC.
newsitem.headline: America Online sees unfair burden from FCC.

text.p: America Online Inc said Wednesday the ruling by the Federal Communications Commission seeking to revamp phone charges will have a disproportionate impact on Internet Service Providers (ISPs).

"While the intent of the FCC was to be broad-based..., we recognize that the provisions announced today will have a disproportionate impact on Internet Service Providers and their consumers," said Steve Case, chairman and chief executive of America Online.
"However, on balance we're prepared to accept these additional costs because the FCC has taken off the table the possibility of additional access charges targeted at Internet use," he said.
The comments followed a ruling by the FCC earlier Wednesday to overhaul domestic telephone charges.

Among its orders, the FCC issued a reduction in the charges long-distance carriers pay local companies to access their networks. It also called for a line charge increase for residential and business customers with more than one phone line.
